absent: Definitions and scaling of vruntime helpers, entity keying, queue averages and weights, fair delta conversion, and queue base values.
Locking, calling context, and runqueue lock requirements for dequeue, hierarchy, entity, lag, pick, stats, and accounting helpers except where stated.
Full struct layouts, field widths, and units for runqueues, fair queues, scheduling entities, tasks, statistics, bandwidth control, domains, and flag sets.
Semantics and numeric values of dequeue flags, update actions, scheduling features, tick constants, load constants, and runtime limits.
Behavior of named but unrouted helpers for current updates, load averaging, buddy handling, running count changes, blocking, enqueue and pick, throttling, bandwidth periods, and balance workhorses.
Concurrency and lifetime rules for leaf list handling, temporary branch repair, pelt clock fields, hrtimer callbacks, and RCU protection.
Misfit, capacity, clamp, and utilization estimation data sources and update timing beyond the instantaneous reads shown.
No complete ABI constant table or lock hierarchy can be fixed from these fragments alone.

findings.text: Entity eligibility is offered as a public check that forwards an entity virtual time to a queue level eligibility predicate.

Eligibility compares a weighted average offset against the scaled distance between candidate time and queue base, folding in the running entity when present, with separate wide arithmetic or overflow fallback behavior by build.

Stored lag is the queue average minus entity time limited symmetrically by a weight scaled bound built from max slice plus one tick, with delayed entities retaining the larger of prior and fresh lag and an optional nonpositive cap, reporting whether average minus lag differs from entity time.
Queue max slice is the larger of the on queue current slice and the tree root maximum, or zero when neither is available.
First and root selection return the entity linked to the leftmost cached node and to the tree root respectively, with null when the structure is empty.

The fair runqueue carries a current entity pointer, timeline tree, weighted sums and base, hierarchical runnable queued and idle counts, idle and throttle clocks, bandwidth and leaf list state, and load and pelt fields touched by dequeue and balance paths.

The scheduling entity carries virtual time and lag, slice limits and deadlines, queue membership and delayed flags, tree and group linkage, hierarchical and instantaneous load, utilization averages, and a back pointer to its queue or owned queue.

Task dequeue clears buddy hints, refreshes current time and lag, parks ineligible sleeping entities in delayed state without hierarchy removal, otherwise removes hierarchy state, converts deadline to relative form for non sleeping paths, erases noncurrent entities from the tree, decrements running count, advances balance timing on transition to idle, and finalizes delayed sleeps with a blocking fixup.

Delayed marking sets a per entity flag and for tasks adjusts preferred cache running state plus decrements hierarchical runnable counts upward, while clearing reverses those adjustments and increments counts upward, with group entities only toggling the flag.

Hierarchy dequeue walks ancestors updating clocks, dequeues the child level then only refreshes upper levels once a parent retains other weight, decrements queued runnable and idle counters, propagates idle status downward, records throttle clocks when throttled, and forces sleep semantics downward while dropping delayed and special marks.

Single level dequeue synchronizes load and runnable state, ends statistics, clears queue membership, subtracts load and queued count, returns surplus runtime, refreshes group share, and when empty snapshots idle pelt time and detaches throttled leaves with pelt clock capture.

Bandwidth return protects shared pool updates with the bandwidth lock while runqueue lock is already held and defers unthrottle work to a timer, while newly idle balance declares a runqueue lock requirement then temporarily unpins and releases it across domain scanning before reacquiring and repinning.

Newly idle balancing updates misfit state, exits early on pending wakeups or inactive processors or cheap idle history, otherwise scans domains within an idle cost budget with optional randomized skipping, tracks domain costs, advances next balance timing, resets idle timestamp on success and delegates to nohz handling on failure.
Slack bandwidth start is skipped when a quota refresh is imminent or already pending, otherwise it marks slack active and arms a relative timer for the slack period.

The eligibility product can exceed signed wide range on some builds, so the design selects wide multiplication or explicit overflow detection with sign based outcome, while narrow builds use native multiplication.

Because idle balancing releases the runqueue lock during scanning, a concurrent arrival can change queue state, so the path rechecks queued and higher class modification state to repair its result before returning.

Misfit load tracking is inert without asymmetric capacity, otherwise it clears the runqueue misfit value for absent pinned maximal or fitting tasks and otherwise stores at least one unit of hierarchical load.
Fit testing combines the larger of instantaneous and estimated utilization with effective minimum and maximum clamp values against target processor capacity.

Idle detection, leaf list removal, NUMA accounting, throttle tests, runtime return, idle pelt update, runnable refresh, and throttle clock recording each have an alternate build that returns a constant or does nothing.
Dequeue statistics end wait timing except for the hierarchical current and record sleep or block start times from task state when enabled, ignoring missing start values caused by late enabling.

Tree removal uses an augmented cached erase plus subtraction of the entity weighted contribution from queue sums, while accounting removal also drops NUMA and cache state, unlinks the group node, and decrements the queued count.
Current time refresh is skipped when no current entity exists and otherwise refreshes through the owner queue, while idle detection is true only when running and idle counts match and are nonzero.
Throttle clock recording captures first throttle and self throttle timestamps from runqueue clock when unset, gated by throttled state for the shared clock.

Surplus return is skipped without bandwidth control or when runtime is disabled or queue remains nonempty, otherwise only positive slack above a minimum is returned to a finite quota pool with deferred unthrottle kick, always consuming the slack locally.
